nodes.name: V-NiS hydrothermal sulfuration
nodes.procedure: V-NiS catalyst was fabricated via Ni foam (NF) in situ sulfuring by a one-step hydrothermal reaction (Figures S1 and S2). The scanning electron microscope (SEM) images reveal that V-NiS possesses a uniform nanorod array structure with an average length of approximately 8 μm.
nodes.source_text: V-NiS and NiS catalysts were fabricated via Ni foam (NF) in situ sulfuring by a one-step hydrothermal reaction (Figures S1 and S2).

nodes.name: NiS hydrothermal sulfuration
nodes.procedure: NiS catalyst was fabricated via Ni foam (NF) in situ sulfuring by a one-step hydrothermal reaction (Figures S1 and S2). NiS exhibits a nanosheet morphology.
nodes.source_text: V-NiS and NiS catalysts were fabricated via Ni foam (NF) in situ sulfuring by a one-step hydrothermal reaction (Figures S1 and S2).

nodes.description: Stability test at high current densities
nodes.source_text: V-NiS demonstrated remarkable stability for 120 h at both 40 and 200 mA cm⁻², as confirmed by chronopotentiometry (Figure 1f)

The cathodic peak of V-NiS obviously shifts negatively (ΔE_cp of about -140 mV)... the number of active sites in V-NiS increases significantly with incremental CV cycles... the electrochemical surface area (ECSA) of V-NiS increased after CV activation
the minor shift of NiS (about 23 mV) is caused by the surface wetting process... that of NiS stayed unaltered (Figure S14)
operando Raman spectra... during the chronopotentiometry measurement at a low current of 0.5 mA... three-step transition process of V-NiS → Ni(OH)₂ → NiOOH

nodes.characterization_summary: V-NiS possesses a uniform nanorod array structure with an average length of approximately 8 μm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscope (SEM) images reveal that V-NiS possesses a uniform nanorod array structure with an average length of approximately 8 μm, whereas NiS exhibits a nanosheet morphology.

nodes.characterization_summary: V-NiS exhibits distinct lattice fringes with an interplanar spacing of 0.32 nm corresponding to the (110) plane of Ni₃S₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM image exhibits distinct lattice fringes, with an interplanar spacing of 0.32 nm corresponding to the (110) plane of Ni₃S₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping images demonstrate the homogeneous distribution of Ni, S, and V in V-NiS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS mapping images demonstrate the homogeneous distribution of Ni, S, and V in V-NiS.

nodes.characterization_summary: Single Ni₃S₂ phase confirmed for V-NiS by XRD patterns (Figure S5).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of a single Ni₃S₂ phase is confirmed by the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns and Raman spectra, thus validating the introduction of V (Figure S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman shows three-step transition V-NiS → Ni(OH)₂ (peak at 488 cm⁻¹) → NiOOH (peaks at 470 and 550 cm⁻¹).
nodes.evidence_snippet: After another 0.5 h, a decreased slope indicates the second-step generation of Ni(OH)₂ on the surface, confirmed by the appearance of a broad Raman peak at 488 cm⁻¹. ... Then the stepwise shaping of two typical peaks at 470 and 550 cm⁻¹ (observed at 2.5 h) demonstrates the massive formation of NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p XPS of V-NiS shows 1.16 eV positive shift after activation indicating Ni³⁺ formation; V 2p undetectable after activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: for V-NiS, a positive peak shift of 1.16 eV is obviously observed, which implies a massive amount of Ni³⁺ was formed via self-reconstruction ... The V element could not be detected in V-NiS after activation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni L-edge XAS shows increased peak intensities for high-valence Ni in V-NiS; V K-edge XANES shifts to higher energy after activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peak intensities of Ni L3 and L2 states in V-NiS increased noticeably, indicating the formation of active high-valence Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: WT-EXAFS shows V-S bonds at 1.37 and 2.33 Å with decreased intensity and widening after activation indicating V-S bond cleavage.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The initial and activated V-NiS exhibit two peaks centered at 1.37 and 2.33 Å attributable to the V-S bonds with two different lengths.

nodes.characterization_summary: V-NiS shows lower R_ct and R_s values than NiS at same potentials indicating enhanced charge transfer and intermediate generation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Remarkably, both R_ct and R_s values of V-NiS were lower than those of NiS at the same potential, indicating enhanced charge transfer and intermediate generation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Hexagonal close-packed (HCP) crystal structure confirmed for V-NiS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The hexagonal close-packed (HCP) crystal structure of V-NiS is confirmed by the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns (Figure S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP confirms presence of V and S ions (as vanadate and sulfate) in V-NiS electrolyte after activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP results of the V-NiS electrolyte indicate the presence of V and S ions, which Raman analysis confirms as vanadate and sulfate ions, respectively (Figure S11).
